story.title: Anthropic's best AI model struggles to attract users as cheaper tools thrive

draft:
Great tech doesn’t guarantee market share.  

Anthropic’s flagship model, Claude 3, consistently outperforms many rivals on nuanced reasoning tasks, yet it’s losing steam to cheaper alternatives like GPT‑4 Turbo and open‑source LLMs. The FT story shows that developers are willing to sacrifice a few percentage points of quality for a fraction of the cost, especially when they can fine‑tune or host models themselves.

What this tells me is that pricing isn’t just a line‑item; it’s a signal of accessibility. When a model’s API fees climb above the marginal value it adds, the ecosystem quickly gravitates toward lower‑cost options that are “good enough.” Anthropic’s premium positioning may work for niche enterprise use cases, but broader adoption demands a more flexible pricing tier or a clear ROI narrative.

I’m curious how other AI teams are navigating this trade‑off. Are you leaning toward the best‑in‑class model regardless of price, or optimizing for cost‑efficiency first?
